STUDYQURAN:9:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r1.claim: Sirr can mean either a secret itself or the hidden or mysterious aspect of something.
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r1.anchor: can mean both the thing kept secret as well as the aspect of a thing

STUDYQURAN:9:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r2.claim: Najwā means conversation among confidants; here it refers to hypocrites' insults about the Prophet and believers.
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r2.anchor: referring to conversations held between confidants, in this case referring to the insults the hypocrites exchange with one another about the Prophet and the believers

STUDYQURAN:9:78/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r3.claim: The unseen consists of real things absent from present sensory perception or belonging to another time or state of being.
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r3.anchor: things that are real but absent from sensory perception in the present moment or absent because they will occur or have occurred at a different moment in time or state of being

STUDYQURAN:9:78/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r4.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r4.claim: Virtuous spiritual people contrast with hypocrites: they accept God's provision and worship and remember Him unseen; their private discourse is worship rather than mockery.
STUDYQURAN:9:78/r4.anchor: virtuous and spiritual persons are the reverse of hypocrites; they are satisfied with what God gives them and worship and remember God when no one can see

TAB-FULL:v11p587/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r1.claim: The hypocrites secretly disbelieve in God and His Messenger while publicly showing belief to believers; God knows their hidden disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r1.anchor: فينهاهم ذلك عن خداع أوليائه بالنفاق والكذب

TAB-FULL:v11p587/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r2.claim: Their private conversations involve attacking Islam and its adherents and speaking of them in improper ways; they should fear God's punishment, desist, and repent.
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r2.anchor: إذا تناجوا بينهم بالطعن في الإسلام وأهله وذكرهم بغير ما ينبغي أن يذكروا به

TAB-FULL:v11p587/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r3.claim: God is the Knower of all that is hidden from created beings' hearing, sight, and senses and remains concealed in their hearts.
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r3.anchor: ما غاب عن أسماع خلقه وأبصارهم وحواسهم مما أكنته نفوسهم

TAB-FULL:v11p587/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r4.claim: Awareness of God's knowledge should stop hypocrites from deceiving His allies through hypocrisy and lies or showing outwardly what contradicts their inward belief.
TAB-FULL:v11p587/r4.anchor: فينهاهم ذلك عن خداع أوليائه بالنفاق والكذب، ويزجرهم عن إضمار غير ما يبدونه وإظهار خلاف ما يعتقدونه

TABATABAI:9:78-80/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:78-80/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:78-80/r2.claim: Al-najwā means concealed or private speech.
TABATABAI:9:78-80/r2.anchor: النجوى الكلام الخفي والاستفهام للتوبيخ والتأنيب

TABATABAI:9:78-80/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:78-80/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:78-80/r3.claim: The question rebukes and reproaches those being addressed.
TABATABAI:9:78-80/r3.anchor: النجوى الكلام الخفي والاستفهام للتوبيخ والتأنيب

TABRISI:9:75-78/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:75-78/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:75-78/r7.claim: Najwa is secret speech; its related verbs include nājā, tanājā, and intajā, and its plural is anjiya. The root suggests distance from others, or alternatively a raised place beyond a flood's reach where speech is private.
TABRISI:9:75-78/r7.anchor: والنجوى الكلام الخفي. يقال: ناجيته وتناجوا وانتجوا

TABRISI:9:77-78/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:77-78/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:77-78/r1.claim: The question rebukes the hypocrites and means that they ought to know God is aware of what they conceal and privately discuss.

TABRISI:9:77-78/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:77-78/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:77-78/r2.claim: “Their secret” is what they hide within themselves, and “their private conversation” is what they say confidentially among themselves.

TABRISI:9:77-78/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:77-78/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:77-78/r3.claim: The plural “unseen things” covers what is absent from bodies and human perception, whether existent or nonexistent, in every respect it can be known; the form is intensive.
TABRISI:9:77-78/r3.anchor: جمع غيب وهو كل ما غاب عن الأجسام

TABRISI:9:77-78/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:77-78/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:9:77-78/r5.claim: The Prophet states that a hypocrite has three signs: he lies when speaking, breaks promises, and betrays a trust; al-Tabrisi says the report is sound.
TABRISI:9:77-78/r5.anchor: صح في الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ELMALILI:9:78/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:78/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:78/r1.claim: Their sirr is what they conceal in their hearts, while their najwa is their whispered conversation; God knows both.
ELMALILI:9:78/r1.anchor: muhakkak Allah sırlarını: kalblerinde gizlediklerini ve fısıltılarını bilir

ELMALILI:9:78/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:78/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:78/r2.claim: The question rebukes the hypocrites: should they not know that God knows the unseen, before daring to commit such acts against Him?
ELMALILI:9:78/r2.anchor: Yani bunu bilmediler mi ki Allah’a karşı o haltlara cür’et ettiler?

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r2.claim: The passage exemplifies contradictions among people whose faith cannot discipline their conduct and points to hypocrisy in its context and timing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r2.anchor: nifak zihniyetine ve münafıkların tutumlarına gönderme yapılmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r8.claim: The phrase about the day they meet God refers to the Day of Resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r8.anchor: “kendi huzuruna çıkacakları güne kadar” diye mâna verilen kısmından maksadın kıyamet günü olduğu anlaşılmaktadır

QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r20.claim: God warns them through His knowledge as He warns them elsewhere through His acts.
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r20.anchor: خوفهم بعلمه كما خوفهم بفعله في أكثر من موضع من كتابه

QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r21.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r21.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r21.claim: Their secret is what no one besides God can see.
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r21.anchor: و { سرهم } ما لا يطلع عليه غير الله

QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r22.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r22.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r22.claim: Their private conversation is what they say confidentially to one another; the term may also include thoughts surveyed by their own souls.
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r22.anchor: و { نجواهم } ما يتسارون بعضهم مع بعض . ويحتمل أن يكون ما لنفوسهم عليه إشراف من خواطرهم

SULAMI:v1p282#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p282#4/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p282#4/r1.claim: The secret is what only the Knower of secrets can see, while private conversation is what the recording angels can see.
SULAMI:v1p282#4/r1.anchor: السر ما لا يطلع عليه إلا عالم الأسرار والنجوى ما يطلع عليه الحفظة

SAMIN-DURR:9:78/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:78/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:78/r1.claim: Most readers have يعلموا in the third person; ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Ḥasan, and al-Sulamī read it as direct address, turning to the believers rather than the hypocrites.
SAMIN-DURR:9:78/r1.anchor: والجمهور على " يعلموا " بالياء من تحت. وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب والحسن والسلمي بالخطاب

QIRAAT-ER:9:78:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:9:78:13#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:9:78:13#1/r1.claim: Al-ghiyūb with kasra and al-ghuyūb with ḍamma are both canonical plural forms of ghayb without a semantic difference; kasra may reflect dialect.
QIRAAT-ER:9:78:13#1/r1.anchor: Vowel variant: kasra on ghayn instead of ḍamma — al-ghiyūb vs. al-ghuyūb; both are canonical plural forms of ghayb

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r7.claim: The interrogative ‘Did they not know?’ rebukes and censures them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r7.anchor: ألم يعلموا هذا استفهام تضمن التوبيخ والتقريع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r8.speaker: علي وأبو عبد الرحمن والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r8.claim: Ali, Abu Abd al-Rahman, and al-Hasan read taʿlamu with second-person address, addressing the believers in a confirming question.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r8.anchor: وقرأ علي وأبو عبد الرحمن والحسن: تعلموا بالتاء، وهو خطاب للمؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r9.claim: On that reading, the verse assures believers that God exposes the hypocrites and gradually makes their concealed state known to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r9.anchor: وأنه تعالى فاضح المنافقين، ومعلم المؤمنين أحوالهم التي يكتمونها شيئا فشيئا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r10.claim: The verse apparently concerns all hypocrites, including those who made and broke the vow; another group restricts it to the covenant breakers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r10.anchor: والظاهر أن الآية في جميع المنافقين من عاهد وأخلف وغيرهم، وخصتها فرقة بمن عاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies their secret as hypocrisy and resolve to break the vow, and their private talk as religious attacks, calling charity a tax, and plotting to withhold it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r11.anchor: فقال الزمخشري: ما أسروه من النفاق والعزم على إخلاف ما وعدوه، وما يتناجون به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r12.claim: Another view takes their secret as concealed hypocrisy and their private talk as denigration of the Prophet and believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r12.anchor: وقيل: أشار بسرهم إلى ما يخفونه من النفاق، وبنجواهم إلى ما يفيضون به بينهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r13.claim: A further explanation distinguishes what some say quietly to one another as their ‘secret’ from what they discuss openly together as their ‘private talk’; the interpretations are close in meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r13.anchor: وقيل: سرهم ما يسار به بعضهم بعضا، ونجواهم ما تحدثوا به جهرا بينهم

ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r1.claim: The subject of 'Did they not know?' may be the hypocrites or those who made a covenant with God.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r1.anchor: أي المنافقون أو من عاهد الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r2.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r2.claim: Ali is reported to have read the verb with second-person ta, addressing the believers; another view takes it as an address to the first group by a shift in person.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r2.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه قرأ بالتاء على أنه خطاب للمؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r3.claim: Taking the address as a second shift in person is strained because the following phrase says God knows their secret and private talk.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r3.anchor: على الالتفات ويأباه قوله تعالى : أن الله يعلم سرهم ونجواهم

ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r4.claim: If the pronouns refer to hypocrites, their secret is concealed hypocrisy and their private talk is mutual slander; if they refer to covenant-makers, the secret is intent to break the pledge and the talk is calling zakat a tax.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r4.anchor: ما أسروه في أنفسهم من النفاق ومن النجوى ما يتناجون به من المطاعن

ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r5.claim: Secret is mentioned before private conversation because, in ordinary perception, knowing what is secret is more awe-inspiring; the ordering can hasten awe or reassurance according to the readings.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r5.anchor: وتقديم السر على النجوى لأن العلم به أعظم في الشاهد من العلم بها

ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r6.claim: The interrogative either rebukes and threatens them for daring such grave acts despite knowing God's awareness, or prompts acknowledgment that He will punish and requite them; naming God explicitly cultivates awe and magnifies the reckoning.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r6.anchor: والهمزة إما للإنكار والتوبيخ والتهديد أي ألم يعلموا ذلك حتى اجترأوا

ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r7.claim: God's being the all-knower of unseen things means nothing at all is hidden from Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r7.anchor: فلا يخفى عليه سبحانه شيء من الأشياء

ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r8.claim: The verb describes God's continually renewed knowledge of successive secrets and conversations, while the intensive nominal form describes enduring, abundant knowledge of innumerable unseen things, giving the sentence force and eloquence.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p145#2/r8.anchor: بصيغة الفعل الدال على الحدوث والتجدد والعلم المتعلق بالغيوب الكثيرة بصيغة الاسم الدال على الدوام والمبالغة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p78#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p78#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p78#2/r1.claim: Their secret is what they conceal in their hearts, and their private conversations are what they discuss among themselves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p78#2/r1.anchor: يعني: ما أضمروا في قلوبهم وما تناجوا به بينهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r7.claim: The implied subject may be hypocrites or those who made a covenant with God; a variant shifts to direct address with tāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r7.anchor: أي المنافقون أو من عاهد الله وقرىء بالتاء على الالتفات

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r8.claim: Their secret is inward hypocrisy or an intention to break their promise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r8.anchor: ما أسروه في أنفسهم من النفاق أو العزم على الإخلاف

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r9.claim: Their private conversations contain attacks among themselves or their labeling zakāh a jizya.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r9.anchor: وما يتناجون به فيما بينهم من المطاعن، أو تسمية الزكاة جزية

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r10.claim: God knows unseen things, so none of this is hidden from Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r10.anchor: علم الغيوب } فلا يخفى عليه ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r6.claim: Their apparent enrichment could mislead the ignorant into thinking God did not know their inward state; judgment of their hearts instead proves He knows every heart better than its owner.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r6.anchor: كان ذلك ادل دليل على أنه تعالى أعلم بما في كل قلب من صاحب ذلك القلب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r7.claim: Their secret is what their breasts conceal.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r7.anchor: { يعلم سرهم } وهو ما أخفته صدورهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r8.claim: Their private talk is what they discuss among themselves; nothing of it is hidden from God.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r8.anchor: { ونجواهم } أي ما فاوض فيه بعضهم بعضا , لا يخفى عليه شيء منه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r9.claim: God is the all-knower of every unseen thing.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r10.claim: Knowing their hidden dealings and consequences, God cannot be deceived; they should fear the outcome and fulfill their covenant.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r11.claim: God's giving despite knowing their betrayal establishes the proof against them.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r11.anchor: وفائدة الإعطاء مع علمه بالخيانة إقامة الحجة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r12.speaker: علي وأبو عبد الرحمن والحسن
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r12.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reports that ʿAlī, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and al-Ḥasan read the question with second-person plural 'a-lam taʿlamū,' addressing the believers as an admonitory report.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r12.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وقرأ علي وأبو عبد الرحمن والحسن { ألم تعلموا } بالتاء , وهو خطاب للمؤمنين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r13.claim: The shift to address believers signals that this knowledge benefits only those prepared for faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p364/r13.anchor: وفائدة الالتفات الإشارة إلى أن هذا العلم إنما ينفع من هيىء للإيمان

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1849#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1849#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1849#2/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says God knows what is more hidden than a secret, including what a person has not yet done but will do.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1849#2/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك يعلم السر قال : يعلم ما هو اخفى من السر مما لم يعمله وهو عامله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p246#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p246#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p246#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cites this verse as a parallel interrogative used to alert listeners to an important matter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p246#3/r3.anchor: ألم يعلموا أن الله يعلم سرهم ونجواهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r4.claim: The opening of this verse is connected to the interpretation that the previous pact was made by intention rather than speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r4.anchor: وقوله: ألم يعلموا الآية، لفظ به تعلق من قال في الآية المتقدمة إن العهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r5.claim: The majority read يعلموا with yāʾ, in the third person.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r6.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Ḥasan read تعلموا with tāʾ, in the second person.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن والحسن «ألم تعلموا» بالتاء، من فوق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r7.claim: The verse rebukes their secret plotting to disparage Islam and their private coordination against the Prophet, his community, and his law; its warning applies to all hypocrites.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r7.anchor: وفيها توبيخهم على ما كانوا عليه من التحدث في نفوسهم من الاجتماع على ثلب الإسلام، وراحة بعضهم مع بعض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r8.speaker: قائل المقالة المذكورة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r8.claim: The interpreter who takes the pact as an inward intention restricts this verse to the group that made that pact.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r8.anchor: وقائل المقالة المذكورة ذهب إلى أنها تختص بالفرقة التي عاهدت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#4/r1.claim: Their secret is what they hold within themselves.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#4/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ألم يعلموا ﴾ يعني المنافقين ﴿ أن الله يعلم سرهم ﴾ وهو ما في نفوسهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#4/r2.claim: Their private conversation is what they say among themselves.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p184/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p184/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p184/r3.claim: God knows their secret thoughts and private talk, their inner motives even when they profess charity, and everything hidden or manifest, unseen or witnessed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p184/r3.anchor: يخبرهم تعالى أنه يعلم السر وأخفى، وأنه أعلم بضمائرهم وإن أظهروا أنه إن حصل لهم أموال تصدقوا منها

JISHUMI:v1p448/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p448/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p448/r1.claim: The passage exposes and warns against the hypocrites’ obstinate rejection: they knew the truth but abandoned it, and its disclosure of their secrets is a sign of the Prophet’s miracle.
JISHUMI:v1p448/r1.anchor: معاندين، علموا الحق وتركوه، وتدل على معجزة

JISHUMI:v1p448/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p448/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p448/r3.claim: Iʿlān means making something manifest or perceptible; it is the opposite of concealment, isrār.

JISHUMI:v1p448/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p448/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وجماعة
JISHUMI:v1p448/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and others say God knows their concealed rejection of Muhammad and their public profession to believers that they have faith.
JISHUMI:v1p448/r6.anchor: من كفرهم بمحمد وما يعلنون يظهرون للمؤمنين من قولهم: إنا آمنا، عن الحسن وقتادة وجماعة

JISHUMI:v1p448/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p448/r7.speaker: أبو علي وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p448/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī and Abū Muslim take the words generally: God knows everything people hide and make public.
JISHUMI:v1p448/r7.anchor: يعلم جميع ما يسرون وما يعلنون، عن أبي علي وأبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v1p448/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p448/r8.speaker: unspecified
JISHUMI:v1p448/r8.claim: Another explanation asks whether they do not know that their deceptions cannot fool one who knows private and public matters.
JISHUMI:v1p448/r8.anchor: أولا يعلمون أن مثل هذه المخاريق لا تروج على من يعلم السر والعلانية

JISHUMI:v1p448/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p448/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p448/r9.claim: Abū Muslim says they should have known from the signs and proofs God established that He knows their private and public affairs.
JISHUMI:v1p448/r9.anchor: بالآيات والدلالة التي أقامها الله تعالى، أن الله يعلم سرهم وعلانيتهم، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v1p448/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p448/r10.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p448/r10.claim: Abū ʿAlī says they should know that the God they already acknowledge knows their secrets and what they make public, showing that they recognized God.
JISHUMI:v1p448/r10.anchor: الله الذي أقروا به يعلم سرهم وجهرهم، عن أبي علي، وهذا يدل على أنهم كانوا عالمين

MUQATIL:9:75-79/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:75-79/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:75-79/r5.claim: The secret and private conversation refers to the plot agreed upon by the people of the Aqaba to kill the Prophet.
MUQATIL:9:75-79/r5.anchor: الذي أجمعوا عليه من قتل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r1.claim: The hypocrites' secret is their hypocrisy and resolve to break their pledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r1.anchor: يعنى المنافقين ﴿ أن الله يعلم سرهم ﴾ أى ما اسروه من النفاق بالعزم على اخلاف ما وعدوه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r2.claim: Their private conversations attack religion, call alms a poll tax, and plan to withhold them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r2.anchor: وما يتناجون به فيما بينهم من المطاعن فى الدين وتسمية الصدقة جزية وتدبير منعها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r3.claim: God knows all unseen things, so nothing is hidden from Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p101/r3.anchor: ﴿ وأن الله علام الغيوب ﴾ فلا يخفى عليه شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r1.speaker: ابن عمرو وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r1.claim: They report that the Prophet explained lying, breaking promises, and betraying trusts as hypocrisy traits, then reassured them and linked each trait to Qurʾanic passages; believers guard the religious trust even in private.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمرو وابن عباس قالا: أتينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في أناس من أصحابه

QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r2.claim: The question is a rebuke: God knows their secrets and private counsels, so He will requite them.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r2.anchor: هذا توبيخ، وإذا كان عالما فإنه سيجازيهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r3.speaker: كثير من التابعين والأئمة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r3.claim: Many Successors and imams adopted the broad interpretation of the hypocrisy traits discussed in the preceding report.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r3.anchor: وإلى هذا صار كثير من التابعين والأئمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r4.speaker: طائفة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r4.claim: One group says the traits designate a person only when they predominate in his character.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r4.anchor: قالت طائفة: هذا فيمن كان الغالب عليه هذه الخصال.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r5.speaker: البخاري وغيره من أهل العلم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r5.claim: The apparent position of al-Bukhari and other scholars is that anyone characterized by these traits remains a hypocrite until the Resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r5.anchor: ويظهر من مذهب البخاري وغيره من أهل العلم أن هذه الخلال الذميمة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says even when sins predominate, they do not make someone an unbeliever unless they affect his belief.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r6.anchor: قال ابن العربي: والذي عندي أنه لو غلبت عليه المعاصي ما كان بها كافرا

QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r7.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r7.claim: The scholars argue that Joseph’s brothers broke a pledge, lied to their father, and betrayed Joseph, yet were not hypocrites.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r7.anchor: قال علماؤنا: إن إخوة يوسف عليه السلام عاهدوا أباهم فأخلفوه،

QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r8.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r8.claim: ʿAta says Joseph’s brothers committed these traits without being hypocrites, since they were prophets.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r8.anchor: قال عطاء بن أبي رباح: قد فعل هذه الخلال إخوة يوسف ولم يكونوا منافقين

QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r9.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن البصري
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r9.claim: Al-Hasan distinguishes hypocrisy of lying, which existed in the Prophet’s time, from hypocrisy of conduct, which continues until the Resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن البصري: النفاق نفاقان، نفاق الكذب ونفاق العمل

QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r10.speaker: حذيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r10.claim: Al-Bukhari reports from Hudhayfa that hypocrisy existed in the Prophet’s time, whereas later it is unbelief after faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r10.anchor: وروى البخاري عن حذيفة أن النفاق كان على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأما اليوم

BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r2.claim: The question is confirmatory: the covenant-makers did know that God knows their secrets and private conversations.
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r2.anchor: أي : من عاهدوا الله والاستفهام للتقرير ، أي قد علموا

BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r3.claim: God knows their hidden resolve to break the promise and their private talk, including calling zakat a tax and other speech devoid of good, whether said secretly or publicly.
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r3.anchor: ما أسروه في أنفسهم من العزم على الإخلاف ولم يتكلموا به سرا ولا جهرا

BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r4.claim: Najwa means conferring a secret; the verb najāhu or nājāhu means speaking privately, and najwa is a secret or confidential speech.
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r4.anchor: والتناجي (بايكديكر راز كردن) يقال نجاه نجوى وناجاه مناجاة ساره

BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r5.claim: The Persian couplet warns against contemplating disobedience when one knows God knows and sees.
BURSEVI:v3p356#3/r5.anchor: مكن انديشه عصيان وميدانى كه ميداند مبين در روى اين وآن وميدانى كه مى بيند

RAZI-FULL:v16p111/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p111/r1.speaker: أصحاب هذا القول
RAZI-FULL:v16p111/r1.claim: One view says a vow includes both a promise spoken aloud and an intention formed silently; its proponents read the passage’s mention of secrets and private counsel as evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v16p111/r1.anchor: أصحاب هذا القول إن قوله : { ومنهم من عاهد الله } كان شيئا نووه في أنفسهم

RAZI-FULL:v16p114/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p114/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p114/r2.claim: Razi rejects that inference: where separate evidence excludes vision in a particular use of meeting, it does not require excluding vision from every other use.
RAZI-FULL:v16p114/r2.anchor: وذلك لأنا تركنا حمل لفظ اللقاء على الرؤية في هذه الآية ، وفي هذا الخبر لدليل منفصل ، فلم يلزمنا ذلك في سائر الصور

RAZI-FULL:v16p114/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p114/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p114/r5.claim: Secret is what breasts conceal; najwā is private discussion among people, from najwa, a secluded elevation or place, since interlocutors exclude others; Razi links 19:52, 12:80, 58:9, and 58:12.
RAZI-FULL:v16p114/r5.anchor: والسر ما ينطوي عليه صدورهم ، والنجوى ما يفاوض فيه بعضهم بعضا فيما بينهم ، وهو مأخوذ من النجوة

RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r1.claim: The warning is that hypocrites dare to conspire despite knowing God sees their hidden and whispered conduct as clearly as the public, and punishes it likewise.
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r1.anchor: إذا عرفت الفرق بين السر والنجوى ، فالمقصود من الآية كأنه تعالى قال : ألم يعلموا أن الله يعلم سرهم ونجواهم

RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r2.claim: ʿAllām intensifies ʿālim; the unseen is what creatures cannot perceive, and God’s essence entails knowledge of every thing, including inner thoughts, so nothing can be hidden from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r2.anchor: والعلام مبالغة في العالم ، والغيب ما كان غائبا عن الخلق . والمراد أنه تعالى ذاته تقتضي العلم بجميع الأشياء

RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r3.claim: Razi compares this divine title with Jesus’ words in 5:116.
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r3.anchor: ونظير لفظ علام الغيوب ههنا قول عيسى عليه السلام : { إنك أنت علام الغيوب }

RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r4.claim: Calling God ʿallāma is improper because the form suggests effortful learning, and effort is impossible for God.
RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r4.anchor: فأما وصف الله بالعلامة فإنه لا يجوز لأنه مشعر بنوع تكلف فيها يعلم والتكلف في حق الله محال
